digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions workflows; CI gate guards
propositions: The shell guard pattern '[ -f <path> ] || { echo "change predates the gate"; exit 0; }' appears 24 times across six CI workflow files and has drifted into inconsistency (two bugs: missing guard in anxious-resistant-urson, guard added late in sapphire-vulnerable-fruitfly).
A shared owner (composite action, shell helper, or Python module) cannot replace the inline guards because it would be absent on pre-gate trees where the guard is needed to prevent false failures.

Three of four gates already share a uniform ref resolver (gate_source.resolve_gate_handle) and a uniform enabled-check function (gate_enabled), making a separate GatePolicy resolver pure indirection with no behavior change or copy removal.

The guard is applied unevenly: test.yml invokes check_readme_quickstart.py and probe_rebar.py without guards, while gerrit-verify.yaml guards the same scripts—reproducing the anxious-resistant-urson bug pattern.
Four workflow steps carry side-effects (output variables, inverted guard logic, data file continuation) that a bare skip would silently drop and require explicit preservation.

The achievable equivalent of consolidation is one owner for the invariant—a parity test asserting every gate step either carries an -f guard for its dependencies or a mandatory-reason # predates-gate-ok: marker, with behavior pinned by running guarded steps in an empty directory.
